comparison: Perfect agreement on p27-SJ403 validation (C41-C45). Both evaluations find the DIRseq predictions for p27 binding motifs are well-supported by CSP data with strong correlation (r=0.82). Reviewers implicitly accept this as part of the validation set across 10 IDPs.

Perfect agreement on p21-SJ403 validation (C46-C49, C51). Both evaluations support DIRseq's ability to distinguish strong and weak binding sites with mechanistic explanation. Reviewers accept this as part of the validation demonstrating aromatic interactions.

Perfect agreement on p53-EGCG validation (C52-C56). Both evaluations find DIRseq predictions are supported by CSP and MD simulation data with good correlation (r=0.67). Reviewers accept this as independent validation on a different IDP-drug system.

Perfect agreement on α-synuclein validation (C57-C64). Both evaluations accept the moderate correlation and interpretation of method limitations. Reviewers acknowledge validation across multiple IDPs and note the method's compound-independent nature as both strength and limitation.

Perfect agreement on parameter optimization (C71, C73, C77-C80). Both evaluations support the systematic comparison showing aromatic-only models are insufficient and final parameters are justified. Reviewers accept the optimization while noting 'ad hoc modifications' without challenging results.

Perfect agreement on aromatic anchoring mechanism (C82-C86). Both evaluations strongly support the role of aromatic interactions in drug binding. Reviewers explicitly emphasize 'solid support through examples underscoring the role of aromatic interactions' as a key finding.

Perfect agreement on DIRseq utility with ambiguous CSP data (C87-C98). Both evaluations support the integration of DIRseq predictions with NMR and MD simulation data to resolve ambiguous cases. Reviewers accept this as demonstrating complementary value of multiple approaches.

Perfect agreement on uncertainty (C99-C104). Both evaluations rate this case as UNCERTAIN due to very weak CSP signals and limited experimental validation. Reviewers implicitly acknowledge 'varying depths' of validation and 'coarse' predictions in some cases.

Perfect agreement on integration with mutational data (C105-C111). Both evaluations support DIRseq predictions validated by mutational analysis. Reviewers accept this as part of validation set demonstrating orthogonal experimental support.

Perfect agreement on short IDP case (C112-C118). Both evaluations support the methodological adjustment for short sequences and partial overlap between DIRseq and CSP. Reviewers accept this as part of the 10 IDP validation set.

Strong agreement on integration with qualitative NMR data (C119-C123). Both evaluations support DIRseq predictions validated by chemical shift movements and peak broadening. OpenEval includes C124 while peer review explicitly lists it; both accept multiple lines of evidence approach.

Perfect agreement on complex multi-site case (C125-C133). Both evaluations support the reanalysis of CSP data with stringent thresholds and DIRseq predictions for multiple binding sites. Reviewers accept this as demonstrating complementary value of methods.

Perfect agreement on main findings and novelty (C134-C138). Both evaluations strongly support the novelty, accuracy, and mechanistic insights. Reviewers emphasize this is 'the first sequence-based prediction method' with 'solid support' and highlight aromatic interaction findings.

Perfect agreement on promiscuity and specificity patterns (C139-C149). Both evaluations accept the documented examples of cross-binding and site-specific binding. Reviewers acknowledge these patterns while noting the compound-independent nature affects specificity predictions.

Strong agreement on practical applications (C151-C160). Both evaluations support the proposed applications for fragment selection and complementary use with other methods. OpenEval separates virtual screening claims (C161-C164) while peer review groups all applications together, but both support practical utility.

Partial overlap on virtual screening applications (C161-C164). OpenEval rates these claims as UNCERTAIN due to lack of experimental validation. Peer review groups these with other applications (C151-C160) and supports practical utility generally, though acknowledges speculative nature of some applications.

Strong agreement on methodological development (C15-C17, C25, C29, C32, C34-C35). Both evaluations support the modifications from SeqDYN to DIRseq. OpenEval provides more detailed assessment of parameter choices while peer review notes method 'builds on authors' previous work' without concerns.

Strong agreement on background and motivation (C1-C12). Both evaluations accept the scientific context establishing need for DIRseq. OpenEval separates background (C1-C12) from conceptual foundation (C13-C16) while peer review groups all context together.

Strong agreement on conceptual foundation (C13-C16). Both evaluations support the R2 overlap observation and mechanistic basis for adapting SeqDYN. Peer review groups these claims with broader background (C1-C12) while OpenEval separates them as distinct conceptual foundation.

OpenEval evaluates computational docking methods (C165-C166) as SUPPORTED standard techniques. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically comment on these methodological details for generating illustrative poses.
